candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXIII.2. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And Sarah died... and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her'. Ephrem reads Abraham's mourning as the legitimate-grief warrant: faith in the resurrection does NOT abolish the legitimate human grief at death. Tewahedo funeral theology preserves Ephrem's balance: mourning is permitted (commanded, even) for forty days; Christian hope reshapes mourning but does not eliminate it. Abraham weeping over Sarah's body authorises every Tewahedo funeral weeping.
